Container.Name: isputnik-games
Container.Overview:
Family games for isputnik.home, in a container of their own. Board games: Dots, Star Battle, Chess, Dominoes and Checkers (Russian draughts), played two on one screen, against the computer, or online between family members, who invite each other and play from any device, phone included. Arcade games: Sputnik Catch and Torpedo Run, with a family high-score table. Everything runs on your server; nothing is sent anywhere.
This is an add-on for isputnik.home and does nothing on its own: it has no sign-in and no pages of its own. Install it beside the isputnik container; the family signs in once, in isputnik.home, and finds Games in its menu, at /games on the same address. Set it up from isputnik.home, on Control panel, Settings, Apps, Games. Before installing, press Generate secret there and copy it (it is shown once); paste it into the Gateway Secret field below, which is required. Once the container runs, enter its address on the same page (http://[your Unraid IP]:4200 as installed here) and press Test connection, which then says Paired. Who may play, and from where (home network only, or anywhere), is chosen on Security, App access. Needs isputnik.home 4.38 or newer.
Container.Changes:
### 2026.11.13 — 0.28.0 A chess computer that learns your level, a coach, draw offers and saved games - **A computer that plays at your level.** Besides Easy, Normal and Hard, the chess computer can be set anywhere from 0 to 100 (Custom, with the rating it plays like), or left to adapt: Adaptive plays at your own chess rating, so each game is about even. It starts from your puzzle rating until you have a few rated games, follows you as you play — win and the next game is harder, lose and it eases off — and "Play again" checks where you stand. A game at a strength counts for your rating against that strength. - **A coach on game review.** When you look back over a finished game, the computer weighs every move against the best one it can find and marks the slips: ?! an inaccuracy, ? a mistake, ?? a blunder. Each side gets a count, the move on screen gets a word ("You played Be2; b5 was a little stronger"), and "Show the better move" puts the board back a move with that move marked. - **Offer a draw online.** In an online chess game either player can offer a draw; the other accepts, declines, or plays on, which declines it. An offer stands until it is answered or taken back, and the same player can offer again after a couple of moves. - **Save a game and come back to it.** "Save and leave" puts a game against the computer or at one screen aside, and the chess page lists the saved ones to continue or delete — several at once, kept on the device. A game on the clock does not lose time while it is saved. - **Your games are easier to find.** "My chess games" is on the games page, and the window at the end of a game has a Review button. - **Fix:** hovering the chosen option in a row of choices made its label disappear in the light themes.
### 2026.11.12 — 0.27.0 Blitz chess, pieces you can drag, and invitations with a QR code - **Chess on the clock.** A new game against the computer, at one screen or online can be played with a clock: 1 minute, 3 minutes with 2 seconds added after each move, 5 or 10 minutes. Each side's first move is free, then the clock runs; whoever runs out loses — or it is a draw, if the other side has nothing left to checkmate with. Online, the server keeps the time, so it is the same on both screens, and a game whose time ran out ends the moment either player looks at it. Undo is off on the clock. Before, chess had no clock at all. - **Drag the pieces.** A piece can now be carried to its square with the mouse or a finger, as well as tapped and then tapped where it goes. The squares it may reach are marked while it is carried; let go anywhere else and it goes back. - **A new games lobby.** Bigger game cards with a Play button across each and an invite button in the corner, a short tip on how to invite, a calmer "Your turn" strip with a mountain-and-planet picture, and arrows on the recent games. On a phone the lobby no longer spills past the edge of the screen — the leaderboard's filters pushed it wider. - **A new invitation window.** Games as picture tiles, a searchable list of members, colours shown as swatches, and the game's own settings — the chess clock among them. - **Invite someone outside the family with a QR code.** The External invite tab now shows the settings beside the link: once it is made, a QR code to scan from a phone across the table, the link to copy, a button that writes the invitation email for you, and how long it works — 1, 7 or 14 days. Choosing the length needs the next isputnik.home release; until then every link works for 14 days, as before. - **Fix:** pressing the button to make a guest link without typing the guest's name did nothing at all; it now says the name is missing and puts the cursor there.
### 2026.11.10 — 0.26.0 Play with no connection, and step back through a chess game - **The games play with no connection.** The first visit after this update stores the whole games app on the device, so the installed iSputnik app opens Games on a plane, or away from the house where the server cannot be reached. It opens as the member who last signed in there, says it is offline, and everything that needs nobody else works: games against the computer, two at one screen, Sputnik Catch, Torpedo Run and Crossmath. Before, the page needed the server just to start and showed "The games are not available". - **Results made offline are not lost.** A finished game against the computer, a chess game kept for review and an arcade score wait on the device and are sent when the server is next reached — tried every half minute and whenever the app comes back into view. An arcade run that could not be sent used to count on that device only. Results stay with the member who made them, even if someone else signs in on the same device first. - **What needs the server says so.** Online matches, chess puzzles, My games and game review show "This needs a connection" instead of an error, and inviting is switched off until the connection is back. A device nobody has signed in on, and a guest, still need the server. - **Chess: step back through the game.** A row under the move list — Start, Back, Play, Forward, End — shows any earlier position of the game being played, all the way to the first move, against the computer, at one screen and online. It only looks: the game stays where it is, pieces move again once you are back at the last move, and Undo is still what takes a move back. Play runs the moves one after another and becomes Stop while it does. Game review has the same row; its Next button is now Forward.
### 2026.11.09 — 0.25.4 Also on Docker Hub - **The image is on Docker Hub too, as isputnikdotnet/isputnik.games.** Every release tag publishes the same image to ghcr.io and to Docker Hub, as isputnik.home's does, and the Docker Hub page shows this README under a description that says what the container is: an add-on for isputnik.home. The Unraid template and the compose file keep pulling from ghcr.io.
### 2026.11.09 — 0.25.3 The 0.25.2 image, built this time - **The 0.25.2 image never reached the registry.** Its build failed on a test of the Torpedo Run page that played a run from a random seed; with some seeds the scripted shots earned a bonus round, and the card then waited for it to be fired in before the run was over and reported, so the test saw no report. The test now plays a fixed seed. This release carries everything 0.25.2 announced.
Container.Requires: Needs the isputnik (isputnik.home) container, version 4.38 or newer, installed on the same server. The games are reached only through it.

Config.Name: Games Port
Config.Description: The port the isputnik container reaches the games on: enter http://[your Unraid IP]:[this port] as the Games address in isputnik.home (Control panel, Settings, Apps). Not for browsers: the games open inside isputnik.home. On br0 with a fixed IP, or on a user-defined network shared with the isputnik container, this mapping is not used and the address is the container's own IP or name with port 4200.

Config.Name: Config & Data
Config.Description: Stores the online matches, scores and the games' own log of events (a small SQLite database). Keep it apart from the isputnik container's appdata. isputnik.home's backups include a copy of it.

Config.Name: Gateway Secret
Config.Description: The secret isputnik.home signs its requests with, so this server knows who is signed in. Make it first, in isputnik.home on Control panel, Settings, Apps, Games (Generate secret; it is shown once), and paste it here. Required: the server refuses to start without one, or with one shorter than 32 characters. Nothing else is set on this container; everything about the games is managed inside isputnik.home.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID the server runs as. It runs unprivileged (not root); on first start it takes ownership of the Config & Data path as this user. 99 (nobody) matches the default owner of an Unraid appdata share - leave it unless your share is owned by a different user.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID the server runs as. 100 (users) matches the default group of an Unraid appdata share - leave it unless your share uses a different group.

Config.Name: Log Level
Config.Description: trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal or silent. At info every request is logged, including each poll for the other side's move; warn keeps only problems. isputnik.home shows this log and the games' own event record under Control panel, Overview, Logs.
